The records concern presidential-level diplomacy and the planning of a prominent political figure’s visit, rather than a military mission or congressional delegation. The visit came as Costa e Silva prepared to succeed Humberto Castelo Branco amid Brazil’s post-1964 military government and the institutional consolidation of the regime. The folder therefore documents U.S.–Brazil relations and White House–Department of State coordination during the transition between the Castelo Branco and Costa e Silva administrations, while reflecting the use of biographic briefing and talking points in official diplomatic protocol.

The document records review of the wording by Ambassador Lincoln Gordon and consideration of how a message from President Lyndon B. Johnson might be read in Brasília. Revisions were preferred that avoided excessive detail, an appearance that Washington was directing negotiations, or an implication of U.S. willingness to support commercial creditors.
